title: Give each counter its own dict

tests.expr: (c := make_counter(), d := make_counter(), c('a'), c('a'), d('a'))[-1]
(c := make_counter(), d := make_counter(), d('x'), d('x'), c('x'), d('x'))[-1]

hints: How many dicts does this program ever make? Count how many times the line `seen = {}` runs.
The line runs once, when the file loads, so every counter writes into the same dict. It should run once for each call to `make_counter()`.
Move `seen = {}` to be the first line inside `make_counter`, indented, above `def count(word):`.
explain: The reference makes the dict inside `make_counter`, so each call to `make_counter()` runs `seen = {}` again and the `count` it returns keeps that fresh dict. In the starter the dict was made once, outside, so every counter shared it.
